```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(ggplot2)
library(plyr)
library(dplyr)
library(grid)
require(gridExtra)
require(lme4)
require(reshape2)
require(ggpubr)
library(cowplot)
library(lmerTest)
source("./../../exp2/analysis/eyetrack.R")

StdErr <- function (x) { return (sd(x)/sqrt(length(x))); }

summarySE <- function(data=NULL, measurevar, groupvars=NULL, na.rm=FALSE,
                      conf.interval=.95, .drop=TRUE, ci = TRUE) {
    library(plyr)

    # New version of length which can handle NA's: if na.rm==T, don't count them
    length2 <- function (x, na.rm=FALSE) {
        if (na.rm) sum(!is.na(x))
        else       length(x)
    }

    if(ci == TRUE)
    {  
    # This does the summary. For each group's data frame, return a vector with
    # N, mean, and sd
    datac <- ddply(data, groupvars, .drop=.drop,
      .fun = function(xx, col) {
        c(N    = length2(xx[[col]], na.rm=na.rm),
          mean = mean   (xx[[col]], na.rm=na.rm),
          sd   = sd     (xx[[col]], na.rm=na.rm)
        )
      },
      measurevar
    )

    # Rename the "mean" column    
    datac <- plyr::rename(datac, c("mean" = measurevar))

    datac$se <- datac$sd / sqrt(datac$N)  # Calculate standard error of the mean

    # Confidence interval multiplier for standard error
    # Calculate t-statistic for confidence interval: 
    # e.g., if conf.interval is .95, use .975 (above/below), and use df=N-1
    ciMult <- qt(conf.interval/2 + .5, datac$N-1)
    datac$ci <- datac$se * ciMult
    }
    else
    {
      
     datac <- ddply(data, groupvars, .drop=.drop,
        .fun = function(xx, col) {
          c(mean = mean   (xx[[col]], na.rm=na.rm))
        },
        measurevar
      )

    # Rename the "mean" column    
    datac <- plyr::rename(datac, c("mean" = measurevar))
    }
    return(datac)
}
```

# Data preparation

Load the raw data where the look is already split in between 4 ROI for each time bin: Target, Distractor, Center, Out of ROI (recorded eye-gaze but not on screen) + Away .

The 0 in the time sequence corresponds to the time (with a few extra ms because of the delay in communication between the eyetracking system and the display computer) where the first look has been initiated during the anticipation period (this time is given online by the experimental script, directly in the output file).

```{r data-load}
data <- read.table("./../data/Results.txt", header = TRUE)
age <- read.table("./../data/age.txt", header = TRUE)
age$group <- "18-24-months-olds (n=30)"
age$group[which(age$Age > 24)] <- "24-30-months-olds (n=20)"
```

Create column Trial_type (known vs. unknown objects) and column block (for trial repetition, max 4 blocks)

```{r data-col}
data$Trial_type <- "known"
data$Trial_type[which(data$Item %in% c("blicket1","nurmy1","meb1","dax1","toma1","blicket2","nurmy2","meb2","dax2","toma2"))] <- "unknown"
data$block <- 1
data$block[which(data$Trial > 10 & data$Trial <= 20)] <- 2
data$block[which(data$Trial > 20 & data$Trial <= 30)] <- 3
data$block[which(data$Trial > 30 & data$Trial <= 40)] <- 4
```

Remove participants that need to be excluded for non-data criteria 

420: parent interfering

428: premature (born 26SA)

```{r participants-selection}
data <- subset(data, !(Subject %in% c(420, 428)))
```

Remove trials that do not folow the following pre-registered criteria:

1. More than 50% of looks on screen during the display period

2. Look initiated during the anticipaton period

3. Took less than 3 seconds to fix the central fixation (time between the display and the anticipation period)

4. More than 50% of looks on screen during the anticipation period

```{r trial-selection}
infos.trials <- ddply(data,.(Subject, Trial, Trial_type, Item, AwayDisp, Tcontingent, Initiated, Tanticipation, Toffset), summarize, away_anticip = sum(Away)/length(Away))
good.trials <- subset(infos.trials, (Initiated == 1 & AwayDisp <= 0.5 & Tcontingent <= 3 & away_anticip <= 0.50))
data <- merge(data, good.trials)
```

Generate sequence of looks for each trial with its associated duration for each ROI. We clean looks that last less than 100 ms as these are likely to be non-elicited by the participant (either on the border of a zone or some flickering due to the eye-tracker; pre-registered criteria).

Below is the number of trials per Trial_type that starts with a given ROI (T,D but also A,C,O) 

```{r trial-sequence}
trial.sequence <- subset(data, Time >= 0)
trial.sequence <- trial.sequence[with(trial.sequence, order(Subject,Trial,Time)), ]
trial.sequence$sequence <- cumsum(c(0,as.numeric(diff(trial.sequence$ROI))!=0))
maxT <- ddply(trial.sequence[with(trial.sequence, order(Subject, Trial,-Time)), ],.(Subject, Trial, Item, ROI, sequence, block, Tanticipation), function(x) x[c(1), ])
maxT <- maxT[, c("Subject","Trial","Item","Trial_type","block","sequence","Time", "ROI","Tanticipation")]
minT <- ddply(trial.sequence[with(trial.sequence, order(Subject, Trial,Time)), ],.(Subject, Trial, Item, ROI, sequence, block, Tanticipation), function(x) x[c(1), ])
minT <- minT[, c("Subject","Trial","Item","Trial_type","block","sequence","Time", "ROI","Tanticipation")]
names(maxT) <- c("Subject", "Trial","Item","Trial_type","block","sequence", "maxTime","ROI","Tanticipation")
names(minT) <- c("Subject", "Trial","Item","Trial_type","block","sequence", "minTime","ROI","Tanticipation")
trial.sequence <- merge(minT, maxT)
trial.sequence$Persistence <- trial.sequence$maxTime - trial.sequence$minTime 
trial.sequence <- subset(trial.sequence, Persistence > 0)
trial.sequence <- subset(trial.sequence, Persistence > 100  | ROI  == "T" | ROI == "D")
trial.sequence <- trial.sequence[with(trial.sequence, order(Subject,Trial,sequence)), ]
trial.sequence$sequence2 <- cumsum(c(0,as.numeric(diff(trial.sequence$ROI))!=0))
trial.sequence <- ddply(trial.sequence, .(Subject, Trial_type, Trial, Item, sequence2, ROI,block,Tanticipation), summarize, minT = min(minTime), maxT = max(maxTime))
trial.sequence$Persistence <- trial.sequence$maxT - trial.sequence$minT 
trial.sequence <- trial.sequence[with(trial.sequence, order(Subject,Trial,sequence2)), ]
trial.sequence <- ddply(trial.sequence, .(Subject, Trial, block), mutate, index=seq_along(sequence2))
ddply(subset(trial.sequence, index ==1), .(Trial_type, ROI), summarize, n = length(Trial))
```

Select first look only to Target or Distractor, greater than 100ms (to avoid some "fake side look" that could be due to a problem of the tracker; pre-registered) and select only participants that have at least 2 trials per Trial_type (pre-registered)

Below:

- the number of participants for each age group (< 2yo and >2yo)

- the proportion of trials used in analysis 

- the average/min/max number of trials + se per participant


```{r first-look-select}
trial.sequence$Tanticipation <- as.numeric(as.character(trial.sequence$Tanticipation))
first.look <- subset(trial.sequence, index ==1 & ROI %in% c("T","D") & Persistence > 100)
known.trials <- ddply(subset(first.look, Trial_type == "known"), .(Subject), summarize, nk = length(unique(Trial)))
unknown.trials <- ddply(subset(first.look, Trial_type == "unknown"), .(Subject), summarize, nu = length(unique(Trial)))
trials <- merge(known.trials, unknown.trials)
first.look <- merge(first.look,trials)
first.look <- subset(first.look, nk > 1 & nu > 1)
#number of participants
length(unique(first.look$Subject))
first.look <- merge(first.look,age)

#Number of participants in each age group:
ddply(first.look, .(group), summarize, n = length(unique(Subject)))
#Proportion of trials in analysis:
print(nrow(first.look)/nrow(infos.trials))
#the average/min/max number of trials + se per participant
first.look %>%
  group_by(Subject)  %>%
  summarize(n_trials = n()) %>%
  group_by()  %>%
  summarize(n_trials_avg = mean(n_trials),
            max_trials = max(n_trials),
            min_trials = min(n_trials),
            se = StdErr(n_trials))

trials.in.analysis <- first.look[c("Subject","Trial","ROI")]
names(trials.in.analysis) <- c("Subject","Trial","first_ROI")
trial.sequence <- merge(trial.sequence, trials.in.analysis)

```

# Analysis 1: Word recognition performance
## First-look responses

### Plots
We first look at the proportion of first target look as a function of trial type:

- averaged over age and block (Fig 1)

- per age (SI)

- per block (SI)

- per Item pair as a function of animacy (symmetric when the pairs of pictures feature two animate or two inanimate objects vs. asymmetric when one object of the pair is animate and the other inanimate)

- early look (< 367ms) vs. later looks (> 367ms)

### statistical analysis


```{r first_look_analysis}
first.look$Age_scaled <- scale(first.look$Age)
m <- glmer(to_target ~ Trial_type * Age_scaled + (1  | Subject), first.look, family= "binomial")

print("test interaction")
m1 <- glmer(to_target ~ Trial_type + Age_scaled + (1  | Subject), first.look, family= "binomial")
print(anova(m,m1))#no


print("test for main effect of age")
first.look$Trial_type <- factor(first.look$Trial_type)
first.look$Trial_type.numeric <- sapply(first.look$Trial_type,function(i) contr.sum(2)[i,])
m2 <- glmer(to_target ~ Trial_type.numeric + Trial_type.numeric:Age_scaled + (1 | Subject), first.look, family= "binomial")
print(anova(m,m2))#yes

print("test for main effect of trial type")
m3 <- glmer(to_target ~ Age_scaled + Trial_type:Age_scaled + (1  | Subject), first.look, family= "binomial")
print(anova(m,m3))#yes

print("comparison to chance")
summary(m)
#We change the intercept in order to have the comparison with the chance level for each condition)
first.look$Trial_type <- factor(first.look$Trial_type)
first.look$Trial_type <- relevel(first.look$Trial_type , "unknown")
m <- glmer(to_target ~ Trial_type * Age_scaled + (1 | Subject), first.look, family= "binomial")
summary(m)


```

### Additional analyses (SI)

Per block

```{r first_look_analysis_block}
#number of participants per block
ddply(first.look, .(block), summarize, n =length(unique(Subject)))

#analysis proper
m <- glmer(to_target ~ Trial_type + block + (1 | Subject), first.look, family= "binomial")
m1 <- glmer(to_target ~ Trial_type + (1 | Subject), first.look, family= "binomial")
print(anova(m,m1))
```

Per RT (>367ms vs. <367ms)

```{r first_look_analysis_RT}
first.look$look <- factor(first.look$look)
first.look$look.numeric <- sapply(first.look$look,function(i) contr.sum(2)[i,])

#interaction
m <- glmer(to_target ~ Trial_type * look + (1  | Subject), first.look, family= "binomial")
m1 <- glmer(to_target ~ Trial_type + look + (1  | Subject), first.look, family= "binomial")
print(anova(m,m1))

#main effect of RT
m2 <- glmer(to_target ~ Trial_type.numeric : look + Trial_type.numeric + (1  | Subject), first.look, family= "binomial")
print(anova(m,m2))

#simple effect for known word
summary(m)

#simple effect for unknown word
first.look$Trial_type <- relevel(first.look$Trial_type , "unknown")
m <- glmer(to_target ~ Trial_type * look + (1  | Subject), first.look, family= "binomial")
summary(m)

d.n <- summarySE(first.look, measurevar="Tanticipation", groupvars=c("Trial_type"))


```

### Statistical analysis 

log transformed raw persistence times 

```{r persistence-analysis}
#dataframe preparation
first.look$Persistence_log <- log(first.look$Persistence)
first.look$Trial_type <- factor(first.look$Trial_type)
first.look$ROI <- factor(first.look$ROI)
first.look$ROI.numeric <- sapply(first.look$ROI,function(i) contr.sum(2)[i,])
first.look$Trial_type.numeric <- sapply(first.look$Trial_type,function(i) contr.sum(2)[i,])

m <- lmer(Persistence_log ~ Trial_type * ROI * Age_scaled + (1   | Subject), first.look)
print("test for triple interaction")
m1 <- lmer(Persistence_log ~ Trial_type.numeric + ROI.numeric + Age_scaled + Trial_type.numeric : ROI.numeric + Age_scaled : Trial_type.numeric + Age_scaled : ROI.numeric + (1   | Subject), first.look)
print(anova(m,m1))  #no

print("test for main effect of Age")
m2 <- lmer(Persistence_log ~ Trial_type.numeric + ROI.numeric + Trial_type.numeric : ROI.numeric + Age_scaled : Trial_type.numeric + Age_scaled : ROI.numeric + Trial_type.numeric : ROI.numeric:Age_scaled +(1   | Subject), first.look)
print(anova(m,m2))  #no

print("test for interaction Age:ROI")
m3 <- lmer(Persistence_log ~ Trial_type.numeric + ROI.numeric + Age_scaled + Trial_type.numeric : ROI.numeric + Age_scaled : Trial_type.numeric  + Trial_type.numeric : ROI.numeric:Age_scaled +(1   | Subject), first.look)
print(anova(m,m3)) #yes

print("test for interaction Age:Trial type")
m4 <- lmer(Persistence_log ~ Trial_type.numeric + ROI.numeric + Age_scaled + Trial_type.numeric : ROI.numeric + Age_scaled : ROI.numeric  + Trial_type.numeric : ROI.numeric : Age_scaled +(1   | Subject), first.look)
print(anova(m,m4))  #no

print("test for interaction between first look and trial type")
m5 <- lmer(Persistence_log ~ Trial_type.numeric + ROI.numeric + Age_scaled + Age_scaled : ROI.numeric  + Trial_type.numeric : ROI.numeric : Age_scaled + Age_scaled : Trial_type.numeric + (1   | Subject), first.look)
print(anova(m,m5)) # yes

print("test for main effect of first look accuracy")
m6 <- lmer(Persistence_log ~ Trial_type.numeric + Trial_type.numeric:ROI.numeric +  Age_scaled + Age_scaled : ROI.numeric  + Trial_type.numeric : ROI.numeric : Age_scaled + Age_scaled : Trial_type.numeric + (1  | Subject), first.look)
print(anova(m,m6)) # yes

print("test for main effect of trial type")
m7 <- lmer(Persistence_log ~ ROI.numeric + Trial_type.numeric:ROI.numeric +  Age_scaled + Age_scaled : ROI.numeric  + Trial_type.numeric : ROI.numeric : Age_scaled + Age_scaled : Trial_type.numeric + (1  | Subject), first.look)
print(anova(m,m7)) #no

#pair-wise comparisons
require(lsmeans)
lsmeans(m, pairwise ~ Trial_type * ROI)
```

```{r persistence-trialtype}
summary(m)
```

## Gaze switch frequency during the anticipation phase

```{r gaze-switch}
d.switch <- merge(trial.sequence,age) %>%
  filter(ROI %in% c("T","D"))%>%
  group_by(Subject, Trial, Trial_type, Age)  %>%
  summarize(n_switch = length(index)) 

df_to_gg_suj <- summarySE(d.switch, measurevar="n_switch", groupvars=c("Subject", "Trial_type"))
df_to_gg <- summarySE(df_to_gg_suj , measurevar="n_switch", groupvars=c("Trial_type"))

dodge= 0.25
gsf <- ggplot(df_to_gg, aes(x= Trial_type, y= n_switch, colour = Trial_type, fill =Trial_type))+ 
  geom_dotplot(data=df_to_gg_suj, binaxis = "y", stackdir = "center", alpha =0.3, position=position_dodge(width=dodge), dotsize = 0.4, binpositions='all' ) + 
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin= n_switch-se, ymax= n_switch +se),width=0.2,size=1,position=position_dodge(width=dodge), colour ="black") +

 scale_colour_manual(values = cmap_cond)  +

print(gsf)
```

### statistical analysis

```{r gaze-switch-analysis}
d.switch$Age_scaled <- scale(d.switch$Age)
d.switch$Trial_type <- factor(d.switch$Trial_type)
d.switch$Trial_type.numeric <- sapply(d.switch$Trial_type,function(i) contr.sum(2)[i,])


print("test for interaction")

print(anova(m,m1))

print("test for main effect of trial type")

print(anova(m,m2))

print("test for main effect of age")

print(anova(m,m2))
```

# Additional plots + analyses 



## test for low level interpretation: RT influence on persistence times (SI)

Could the persistence effect be caused by some low-level response such as RT?

```{r rt,warning=FALSE, message =FALSE}
df_to_gg_suj <- summarySE(first.look, measurevar="Tanticipation", groupvars=c("Subject", "Trial_type","ROI"))
df_to_gg <- summarySE(df_to_gg_suj , measurevar="Tanticipation", groupvars=c("Trial_type","ROI"))

ggplot(df_to_gg, aes(x= Trial_type, y= Tanticipation, colour = ROI))+  geom_line() +geom_point() + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin= Tanticipation-se, ymax= Tanticipation +se), width=0.1) + theme_bw(base_size = 16) + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) + scale_x_discrete(name="Trial type") + scale_y_continuous(name="RT (ms)") +guides(colour=guide_legend(title="First look")) + scale_colour_manual(values = cmap)  + scale_colour_manual(values = cmap,labels = c("Incorrect", "Correct"))  

```

```{r rt-analysis}

print("test main effect of RT")
m <- lmer(Persistence_log ~  ROI * Trial_type + Tanticipation * Trial_type + (1   | Subject), first.look)
m1 <- lmer(Persistence_log ~  ROI * Trial_type + (1   | Subject), first.look)
print(anova(m,m1))

print("test that the interaction is still there when adding RT in the model")
m2 <- lmer(Persistence_log ~ Tanticipation + Trial_type + ROI + (1 | Subject), first.look)
print(anova(m,m2))

print("test that the effect of first look accuracy is still there when adding RT in the model")
m3 <- lmer(Persistence_log ~ Tanticipation +Trial_type.numeric + Trial_type.numeric:ROI + (1 | Subject), first.look)
print(anova(m,m3))
```

## test for low level interpretation: Effect of word-referent knowledge/memory on first looks (SI)

First look responses may be correlated with different states of knowledge about the word. For instance it could be that children who initiated an incorrect first look when tested on a word w knew w less well than children who initiated a correct first look when tested on w (despite parental reports being similar). In other words, looking first at the correct vs. incorrect referent may artificially split our participants according to the strength of their word-referent knowledge. If this is the case, then we would expect that participants who had made a correct first look during the anticipation phase would also have spent more time looking toward the target during the previous looking-while-listening phase, as compared to participants who made an incorrect first look. 

Plot proportion of target looks during the looking-while-listening phase as a function of first look accuracy for known words in the anticipation phase 

```{r display-first-look,warning=FALSE, message =FALSE}
cmap_first <- c("red","blue")
trials <- first.look[, c("Subject","Trial","to_target","Persistence")]
ddisplay <- merge(ddisplay, trials)

df_to_spag <- summarySE(subset(ddisplay, (bin_target != 0 | bin_distractor != 0) & Trial_type == "known"), measurevar="bin_target", groupvars=c("Subject","Time","to_target"),na.rm=TRUE)

display.firstacc <- spaghetti(df_to_spag,meltids=c("TimePlot","Subject","to_target"),meltfactors=c("Subject","to_target"),region=c("bin_target"),colorvariable="to_target", errbarvars=c("to_target"),upperlimit=5000,lowerlimit=0,srate=50,sample=1,downsample="down",timeAlignVar= "Time",onset=0, showplot=T, analysiswindow= T, analysisonset=0,title="",colormapping = cmap_first, area = "",ymax=0.8)+
  guides(fill=guide_legend(title="First look")) + 
  guides(colour=FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cmap_first,labels = c("Incorrect", "Correct"))
print(display.firstacc)
```

## test for low level interpretation: Effect of object preference on persistence times. (SI)

Could it be that children simply persist for longer when they first look towards the object they prefer? 

To test this, we added ObjectPreference (the proportion of target looks during the pre-target word period during the looking-while-listening phase for a given trial) as a predictor in the mixed model analysis of confidence

```{r attentional-bias}
df.trial <- summarySE(subset(ddisplay, (bin_target != 0 | bin_distractor != 0) & Time <=700), measurevar="bin_target", groupvars=c("Subject","Trial","to_target", "Trial_type"),na.rm=TRUE)
df.trial$bin_target_scaled <- scale(df.trial$bin_target)
first.look <- merge(df.trial, first.look)

m <- lmer(Persistence_log ~ Trial_type * ROI * bin_target_scaled + (1   | Subject), first.look)
print("test for triple interaction")
m1 <- lmer(Persistence_log ~ Trial_type.numeric + ROI.numeric + bin_target_scaled + Trial_type.numeric : ROI.numeric + bin_target_scaled : Trial_type.numeric + bin_target_scaled : ROI.numeric + (1   | Subject), first.look)
print(anova(m,m1))  #no

print("test for main effect of perf")
m2 <- lmer(Persistence_log ~ Trial_type.numeric + ROI.numeric + Trial_type.numeric : ROI.numeric + bin_target_scaled : Trial_type.numeric + bin_target_scaled : ROI.numeric + Trial_type.numeric : ROI.numeric:bin_target_scaled +(1   | Subject), first.look)
print(anova(m,m2))  #no

print("test for interaction perf:ROI")
m3 <- lmer(Persistence_log ~ Trial_type.numeric + ROI.numeric + bin_target_scaled + Trial_type.numeric : ROI.numeric + bin_target_scaled : Trial_type.numeric  + Trial_type.numeric : ROI.numeric:bin_target_scaled +(1   | Subject), first.look)
print(anova(m,m3)) #no

print("test for interaction perf:Trial type")
m4 <- lmer(Persistence_log ~ Trial_type.numeric + ROI.numeric + bin_target_scaled + Trial_type.numeric : ROI.numeric + bin_target_scaled : ROI.numeric  + Trial_type.numeric : ROI.numeric : bin_target_scaled +(1   | Subject), first.look)
print(anova(m,m4))  #no

print("test for interaction between first look and trial type")
m5 <- lmer(Persistence_log ~ Trial_type.numeric + ROI.numeric + bin_target_scaled + bin_target_scaled : ROI.numeric  + Trial_type.numeric : ROI.numeric : bin_target_scaled + bin_target_scaled : Trial_type.numeric + (1   | Subject), first.look)
print(anova(m,m5)) # yes

print("test for main effect of first look accuracy")
m6 <- lmer(Persistence_log ~ Trial_type.numeric + Trial_type.numeric:ROI.numeric +  bin_target_scaled + bin_target_scaled : ROI.numeric  + Trial_type.numeric : ROI.numeric : bin_target_scaled + bin_target_scaled : Trial_type.numeric + (1  | Subject), first.look)
print(anova(m,m6)) # yes

print("test for main effect of trial type")
m7 <- lmer(Persistence_log ~ ROI.numeric + Trial_type.numeric:ROI.numeric +  bin_target_scaled + bin_target_scaled : ROI.numeric  + Trial_type.numeric : ROI.numeric : bin_target_scaled + bin_target_scaled : Trial_type.numeric + (1  | Subject), first.look)
print(anova(m,m7)) #no

```
